newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: NAB sees continued margin pressure.
newsitem.headline: NAB sees continued margin pressure.

text.p: National Australia Bank Ltd said on Thursday after posting flat third quarter profit results it expected continued pressure on margins in Australia and it would have to move quickly to better balance interest and fee income.

"The continued pressure on margins in Australia means we will have to quickly address the need to gain a better balance between interest and non-interest or fee income," NAB Managing Director Don Argus said in a statement.
"We will also need a renewed focus on labour and other operating costs here," he said.
NAB announced a third quarter net profit of A$504 million for the three months to June 30, compared with A$505 million in the same quarter a year earlier.
The profit was 15 percent down on the March quarter.
But NAB also reported a 9.3 percent rise in net profit to A$1.643 billion for the nine months to June compared with A$1.50 billion for the previous corresponding period.
The third quarter results saw an immediate reaction from the market, with shares in Australia's biggest bank falling over two percent.
NAB shares were down 50 cents at 12.40 p.m. (0240 GMT) to A$19.00 with 2.9 million shares traded. The shares were trading at A$19.45 before the announcement of the results.
The bank pointed to a good performance from its international operations in explaining the 9.3 percent boost in its profits for the nine months to June.
The profit contribution from overseas increased to 38.3 percent from 31.9 percent a year earlier.
But the bank said its Australian results were flat, with profits for the nine months falling to A$1.01 billion for the nine months from A$1.02 billion a year earlier.
"The strong performance of Europe and other international operations offset what is an extremely competitive operating environment in Australia," Argus said.

On the Australian front, brokers said the third quarter results were well below expectations, adding the share price fall was likely to get the bank's halted share buy-back scheme put back onto the agenda.
NAB said its underlying profitability had improved 7.9 percent to A$2.75 billion from $A2.55 billion in the previous period.
Earnings per share rose 7.1 cents to 111.2 cents from 104.1 cents.
Net interest income rose 3.5 percent to A$3.91 billion from A$3.76 billion while non-interest income rose 12.7 percent to A$2.43 billion from A$2.16 billion.
The bank said lending volumes had continued to grow strongly, particularly in fixed rate business products, leasing and housing.
Its asset base expanded 17.6 percent from the period to June 1996 to more than A$200 billion, the bank said.
